examples.en: I’m all ears—tell me what happened.

meaning.en: To be ready, interested and eager to listen carefully to what somebody is saying or is about to say.
meaning.zh: 準備好並有興趣地專心聆聽某人正在說或即將要說的內容；全神貫注地聽；洗耳恭聽。
naturalZh: 準備好並有興趣地專心聆聽某人正在說或即將要說的內容

register.summaryEn: everyday conversation; friendly messages; classroom discussion; team meetings; interviews; supportive personal conversations.
register.summaryZh: 這個表達屬於非正式至中性語氣，尤其適合日常對話、朋友之間的訊息、課堂討論、團隊會議、面試及支持別人的談話。
register.formalEn: It is friendly and interested rather than rude or demanding. In highly formal academic, legal or technical writing, listen carefully, pay close attention or give full attention may be more suitable. The informal classification is supported by both Collins and Oxford learner dictionaries.
register.formalZh: all 和 ears 必須按照這個次序連在一起使用。

benefits.titleEn: It Naturally Invites Somebody to Continue
benefits.en: The idiomatic version gives the other person a clear and friendly invitation to continue.
benefits.zh: 慣用語版本可以清楚而友善地邀請對方繼續說下去。

benefits.en: I’m all ears does not merely mean that sound can be heard. It shows that the listener wants to understand the message.
benefits.zh: 不只是表示能夠聽到聲音，還表示聆聽者真心希望了解對方的內容。
這個慣用語可以把「已準備好」、「有興趣」及「會專心聆聽」濃縮成一個簡潔的表達。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Describe Both Responses and Situations
benefits.titleZh: 既可用作回應，也可描述情境
benefits.en: The class was all ears when the visitor began speaking.
benefits.zh: 它既可以直接回應另一位說話者，也可以描述某人或一群人專心聆聽的情況。

benefits.titleZh: 營造支持和接納的語氣
benefits.en: When somebody is nervous about sharing an idea or concern, I’m all ears can show patience, openness and support. This idiom is a useful alternative, but it is not automatically better than listen carefully or pay attention. Use it only when its friendly and interested tone suits the situation.
benefits.zh: 當某人對分享想法或憂慮感到緊張時，I’m all ears 可以表達耐心、開放及支持。 這個慣用語是一個實用的替代說法，但並非必定比 listen carefully 或 pay attention 更好。 只有當它友善而有興趣的語氣適合相關情境時，才應使用。

origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成；確切來源不明

history.en: Merriam-Webster records a first known use of all ears with the meaning “eagerly listening” in 1577. A first known written record does not necessarily identify the person who invented the expression or the first time it was ever spoken.
history.zh: 韋氏詞典把 all ears 以「熱切聆聽」意思出現的最早已知用法追溯至1577年。 不過，最早已知的書面記錄不一定代表我們知道是誰創造這個表達，也不一定是它首次在口語中出現的時間。

history.en: In the expression, all suggests complete attention, while ears represent the act of listening. The exaggerated physical image therefore developed naturally into the figurative meaning of listening with complete interest and attention.
history.zh: 在這個表達中，all 表示全部注意力，而 ears 則代表聆聽。 這個誇張的身體畫面因而自然演變成 「帶着充分興趣並全神貫注地聽」的比喻意思。

origin.memoryEn: Imagine that your whole body has turned into ears: every part of you is concentrating on what the other person is saying.
origin.memoryZh: 想像你的全身都變成耳朵：你整個人都正在專心聽對方說話。

rules.titleEn: Use the Correct Form of Be
rules.en: Use the Correct Form of Be

rules.titleZh: 規則二：ears 必須使用複數
rules.en: The singular form appeared in some older literary writing, but it is not the modern target taught in this exercise.
rules.zh: 單數形式曾在部分較古老的文學作品中出現，但並不是本練習教授的現代標準形式。

rules.titleEn: Use It for Interested and Attentive Listening
rules.titleZh: 規則四：用於有興趣及專心的聆聽
rules.en: The second sentence merely describes hearing a sound. It does not show that the speaker is willingly and attentively listening to somebody.
rules.zh: 告訴我你的新想法吧。 我洗耳恭聽。 第二句只表示聽到聲音，沒有表示說話者願意專心聽某人說話。

examples.en: Tell me about your new idea. I’m all ears.
examples.zh: 告訴我你的新想法吧。我洗耳恭聽。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Accidental Overhearing
rules.titleZh: 規則五：不可用來表示無意中聽到
rules.en: If the listening is accidental or secret, heard, overheard or listened in may be more accurate.
rules.zh: 如果只是無意中或秘密聽到別人的說話，使用 heard、overheard 或 listened in 會更準確。

rules.titleEn: The Listener Must Be Genuinely Attentive
rules.titleZh: 規則六：聆聽者必須真正專心
rules.en: does not want to listen; is ignoring the speaker; is paying attention to something else; has already stopped listening.
rules.zh: 如果某人不願意聽、正在忽視說話者、專注於其他事情，或已經停止聆聽，就不應使用這個慣用語。

rules.titleZh: 規則七：自然使用，不要過度使用
rules.en: If the sentence only means that a person can physically hear a sound, ordinary hear or listen is usually better.
rules.zh: 如果句子只表示某人能夠聽到聲音，直接使用 hear 或 listen 通常會更自然。

instructions.en: The first word of each canonical answer has been provided.
instructions.zh: 使用 be all ears 的正確形式改寫句子或完成回應。

questions.answer: Take your time—I’m all ears.
